{{Quote|<nowiki />''[Kossak Inijic Ar'durv's]'' strategies of sabotage and subterfuge are practiced by Huttlets and clans ''[sic]'' leaders alike, and are believed to have inspired Budhila Hestilic Amura's kajidic philosophy.|Professor S. V. Skynx, ''The Despotica Reader'', Third Edition|<ref name="Despotica">{{Hyperspace|url=fans/hyperspace/source/ximweek02/index.html|text=Xim Week: ''The Despotica'' (Part I)|int=Xim Week: The Despotica}}</ref>}}
'''Budhila Hestilic Amura''' was a [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]] from the [[Hestilic]] clan who lived at the beginning of the [[Kymoodon Era]]. Around [[15,000 BBY/Legends|15,000 BBY]], Budhila Hestilic Amura served as the primary [[Diplomat/Legends|negotiator]] on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Nal Hutta/Legends|Evocar]], which the Hutts [[Colonist/Legends|settled]] after leaving their ruined [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], [[Varl/Legends|Varl]]. To prevent a repeat of the [[Hutt Cataclysms]], Budhila developed the [[Philosopher/Legends|philosophy]] known as [[Kajidic/Legends|kajidic]]. It called for the Hutts to reject outright war and conquest through force in favor of gaining control over organizations and worlds via indirect influence. To enforce the concept and govern the Hutt society, Budhila also established the Hutt [[Grand Hutt Council/Legends|Council of Elders]]. [[Millennium/Legends|Millennia]] later, [[Budhila Plaza]] on Nal Hutta's [[Moon/Legends|moon]], [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]], had been named after the creator of kajidic.

==Biography==
===A new homeworld&hellip;===
[[File:HuttSpace15kto12kBBY-EGTW.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Budhila Hestilic Amura lived around 15,000 BBY, during the time when Hutts relocated their homeworld from Varl to Nal Hutta.]]
Budhila Hestilic Amura was a [[Hutt/Legends|Hutt]]<ref name="TORE" /> living at the beginning of the [[Kymoodon Era]], a period of [[Time/Legends|time]] lasting from approximately [[15,000 BBY/Legends|15,000 BBY]]<ref name="TEA" /> to around [[12,000 BBY/Legends|12,000 BBY]].<ref name="EGTW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> He<ref name="TORE" /> was a part of the [[Hestilic]] clan,<ref name="TEA" /> of which another member had been [[Boonta Hestilic Shad'ruu/Legends|Boonta Hestilic Shad'ruu]], a renowned military [[Commander/Legends|commander]] who had led Hutt forces to [[Third Battle of Vontor|victory]] over the [[Tionese (group)/Legends|Tionese]] ruler [[Xim/Legends|Xim]] around [[25,100 BBY]].<ref name="EGTW" />

Budhila lived during a time of disarray for the Hutt [[Species/Legends|species]]. By 15,000 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|BBY]],<ref name="TEA" /> the [[Hutt Empire]] had collapsed at the end of a series of calamities and conflicts known as the [[Hutt Cataclysms]], which saw [[Varl/Legends|Varl]], the species' once-lush [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]], become barren and lifeless. In the aftermath of those catastrophes, a few of the surviving powerful Hutt clans gathered their remaining [[Slavery/Legends|slave]] species to aid them in [[Colonist/Legends|colonizing]] a new homeworld. Rediscovering [[Nal Hutta/Legends|Evocar]]<ref name="TORE" />&mdash;a lush [[Planet/Legends|planet]] settled by the Hutts<ref name="LoNH">''[[Lords of Nal Hutta]]''</ref> [[Standard century/Legends|centuries]] earlier but left in the control of its natives, the peaceful [[Evocii]]<ref name="TEA" />&mdash;the Hutt clans traveled en masse to Evocar<ref name="LoNH" /> aboard the remnants of the Hutt Empire's [[Fleet/Legends|fleet]].<ref name="TORE" /> The Hutts and their [[Vippit]] servants<ref name="TEA" /> then traded trinkets and useless pieces of<ref name="TORE" /> high technology equipment to the Evocii in exchange for huge expanses of land, and soon, the arrivals controlled almost the entire planet, which was remade into a new Hutt homeworld and renamed "Nal Hutta." The Evocii were subsequently enslaved and largely relocated to the planet's [[Moon/Legends|moon]], [[Nar Shaddaa/Legends|Nar Shaddaa]].<ref name="LoNH" />

===&hellip;and a new philosophy===
[[File:HuttaNarShaddaa_TOR.png|thumb|right|200px|Budhila Hestilic Amura served as the primary negotiator on Nal Hutta.]]
Around the time of the Hutt settlement of Nal Hutta, Budhila Hestilic Amura served as the primary [[Diplomat/Legends|negotiator]] on the planet.<ref name="TORE" /> In order to prevent a repeat of the Hutt Cataclysms,<ref name="LoNH" /> Budhila drew inspiration from the Hutt acquisition of Nal Hutta from the Evocii&mdash;which the former species viewed as a lesson in entrepreneurship<ref name="TORE" />&mdash;in order to develop the [[Philosopher/Legends|philosophy]] known as [[Kajidic/Legends|kajidic]]. The name of the concept in [[Huttese/Legends|Huttese]] literally meant "the means by which we prosper," but it was also related by the Hutts to their saying, "Someone's got to have it, why not us?"<ref name="LoNH" /> [[Millennium/Legends|Millennia]] later, [[Professor/Legends|Professor]] [[S. V. Skynx/Legends|S. V. Skynx]] noted in the [[The Despotica Reader, Third Edition|third edition]] of ''[[The Despotica Reader]]'' that it was believed Budhila was also inspired in the creation of the kajidic by the [[Saboteur/Legends|sabotage]] and subterfuge strategies employed by Hutt [[Clan-General]] [[Kossak Inijic Ar'durv]], who had led the overall Hutt [[Xim Wars|campaign]] against Xim.<ref name="Despotica" />

Kajidic called for the Hutts to favor aggressive but non-military internal rivalries, rejecting outright war and territorial conquest. The philosophy also taught the Hutts to dedicate themselves to gaining control over organizations<ref name="LoNH" /> and worlds, such as those of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]],<ref name="TEA" /> through indirect methods in order to achieve rule from within.<ref name="LoNH" /> In order to enforce kadijic, govern the Hutt society, and prevent it from repeating the mistakes that had doomed the Hutt Empire, Budhila also established the body known as the [[Grand Hutt Council/Legends|Council of Elders]], which consisted of five members of the [[Clans of the Ancients|oldest Hutt Clans]].<ref name="TORE" />

Over time, kajidic became so ingrained in Hutt culture that the traditions of the Hutt Empire times became known as the [[Old Ways (Hutt)|Old Ways]] and relegated to myths. Eventually the term "kajidic" was so intertwined with the Hutt clans that the two concepts sometimes became synonymous.<ref name="LoNH" /> By [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]],<ref name="19 BBY">{{StoryCite|story=Lone Wolf: A Tale of Obi-Wan and Luke|book=SkyeWalkers: A Clone Wars Story}} is set in the immediate aftermath of [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'']], the events of which are dated to [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]] by ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''.</ref> the name of the creator of kajidic<ref name="TEA" /> had been immortalized in the name of [[Budhila Plaza]], a location on Nar Shaddaa.<ref name="LoneWolf">{{StoryCite|story=Lone Wolf: A Tale of Obi-Wan and Luke|book=SkyeWalkers: A Clone Wars Story}}</ref>

==Personality and traits==
Budhila Hestilic Amura was an insightful individual who did not wish for his people to return to the excesses and chaos of the fallen Hutt Empire.<ref name="TORE" />

==Skills and abilities==
Budhila Hestilic Amura had sufficient diplomatic skills to serve as the primary negotiator on Nal Hutta around the time of the Hutt settlement of the world.<ref name="TORE" />

==Behind the scenes==
Budhila Hestilic Amura was created for the [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'', authored by [[Daniel Wallace]] and [[Jason Fry]].<ref name="TEA" /> The Hutt's name was derived from two [[Wikipedia:Sanskrit|Sanskrit]] words related to wisdom.<ref name="Atlas endnotes">{{Blogspot|subdomain=geekosity|url=2009/08/endnotes-for-star-wars-essential-atlas_24.html|name=Daniel Wallace's Geekosity|text=Endnotes for Star Wars: The Essential Atlas (part 2 of 5)}}</ref>
